newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Chelsea (7) v Derby (13)

Striker Gianluca Vialli has been told to fight his way back after failing to regain his place following injury and illness. Fellow-Italian international Gianfranco Zola and Welsh striker Mark Hughes are expected to continue in attack in Ruud Gullit's squad, unchanged despite defeat at Nottingham Forest.

Derby aim to win their first game in six. Manager Jim Smith has striker Ashley Ward available after a slight Achilles tendon injury while defender Dean Yates is out for six weeks with a knee ligament injury.
Coventry City (15) v Manchester United (2)

Striker-turned-defender Dion Dublin is banned for seven matches after two successive dismissals and faces the possibility of a heavy fine from the club. Coventry coach Gordon Strachan has mounting problems after last week's 4-0 defeat at Blackburn and has delayed selection decisions.

Champions United, unbeaten in 10 league games, will be without defenders David May, out for six weeks after a hernia operation, and Phillip Neville, who is recovering from glandular fever. Manager Alex Ferguson may be forced to change his formation.
Leicester (16) v Wimbledon (5)

Leicester will be aiming for their first win in five games to stop their slide. Manager Martin O'Neill has signed defender Matt Elliott from first division club Oxford for a club record 1.6 million pounds ($2.7 million) to strengthen the side.
Wimbledon striker Marcus Gayle is doubtful with a groin strain. The London side have lost only once in their last 24 games and remain unexpected title challengers.
Liverpool (1) v Aston Villa (6)

The leaders will be without Ireland defender Phil Babb and midfielder Michael Thomas who are beginning two-match suspensions. England defender Mark Wright is likely to return after a stomach bug but midfielder John Barnes has a hamstring injury.

Villa will be out to avenge two defeats in the league and one in the F.A. Cup last season in their attempt to close the seven-point gap between the two sides. They are feeling the strain as they go into their sixth fixture in a seven-game run of clashes with the top eight sides. Portuguese defender Fernando Nelson, midfielder Ian Taylor and Trinidadian international Dwight Yorke are suffering from thigh strains.
Middlesbrough (20) v Sheffield Wednesday (8)

Bottom club Middlesbrough were dealt a severe blow in midweek when they were docked three points by the Football Association for their unilaterlal decision to withdraw from playing at Blackburn, because of illness and injuries, before Christmas.

Manager Bryan Robson is helped by new signings defender Gianluca Festa from Inter Milan and Vladimir Kinder from Slovan Bratislava. Defender Neil Cox and midfielder Craig Hignett will be missing through suspension.

Sheffield Wednesday are unbeaten in 13 games and could be boosted by the return of two long-term absentees. Defender Jon Newsome is fit after a knee injury and midfielder Wayne Collins could start after four months out with a groin problem. Striker Andy Booth is expected to be fit after a hamstring injury.
Southampton (19) v Newcastle United (4)

Newcastle boss Kenny Dalglish will be in charge for his first league game after seeing his new side give him a winning start in a 2-1 F.A. Cup victory over Charlton on Wednesday. England striker Les Ferdinand returns after a calf strain and former England midfielder Robert Lee is back after suspension as Dalglish pits his wits against his old Liverpool team mate Graeme Souness.

Southampton moved off the bottom of the table with a 1-0 victory at fellow-strugglers Middlesbrough last week. Souness will be without suspended duo of defender Francis Benali and midfielder Robbie Slater.
Sunderland (11) v Blackburn Rovers (14)
Sunderland manager Peter Reid has a catalogue of injuries as his side aim to recover from a 2-0 defeat by Arsenal on Wednesday in the F.A. Cup.

A good home record of only two defeats in 11 games and the return of striker Alex Rae after suspension could be his salvation. Defender Kevin Ball (broken jaw), midfielders Paul Bracewell (calf), Martin Scott (groin), Steve Agnew (wrist) and striker Michael Bridges (groin) are all unlikely to figure.
Blackburn have drawn six out of 11 games away. Midfielder Billy McKinlay is banned through suspension in an otherwise unchanged side.
Arsenal (3) v Everton (9) (Sunday 1600 GMT)
Arsenal coach Arsene Wenger will welcome the return of premier league top scorer Ian Wright from suspension but Welsh striker John Hartson faces the second part of his two-match ban.

Everton's 900,000-pound ($1.5-million) signing Claus Thomsen will make his debut in a weakened midfield. The Danish international will take the place of the injured John Ebbrell. Defenders Dave Watson and Earl Barrett face late fitness tests.
Nottingham Forest (18) v Tottenham Hotspur (10) (Sunday 1600 GMT)

Caretaker player-coach Stuart Pearce aims for a third consecutive victory after a morale-boosting victory over Chelsea last week. Strikers Dean Saunders (hamstring) and Kevin Campbell (groin) are his only doubts.
Tottenham manager Gerry Francis was dealt a blow when Scandanavian pair Allan Neilsen and Steffen Iversen joined the injury list with influenza.
West Ham United (17) v Leeds United (12) (Monday 2000 GMT)
Coach Harry Rednknapp is relatively untroubled on the injury front as his side aim to improve on five points in their last six games.

Leeds broke a spell of three defeats with a 3-0 victory over Leicester last week and aim to continue in that vein. Midfielder Lee Sharpe is due back after a groin strain and Gunnar Halle returns from suspension.
